title: Recognizing a singular total object in a bounded purchase
summary: Recognize the -n total-object form in a completed affirmative purchase: Ostan kirjan (“I will buy a book”).
targetSkills: Recognizing a singular total object in a bounded purchase
prerequisiteSkills: Location postpositions with a singular genitive
objectives: Recognize the -n total-object form in a completed affirmative purchase: Ostan kirjan (“I will buy a book”).

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: These examples describe a planned purchase completed with one whole item obtained. With an ordinary subject in an affirmative active clause, this singular total object has the same shape as the genitive.
The object answers what will be bought; it does not identify an owner. In this use, the label “genitive-shaped total object” describes the form.

Ostan is supplied. Noun models: kirja → kirjan, auto → auton, lelu → lelun, kynä → kynän, laukku → laukun, puhelin → puhelimen, avain → avaimen, pallo → pallon. Affirmative sentences do not always take this object form: ongoing, unbounded, negative and other constructions require separate lessons.
keyPoints: Do not interpret this object as an owner.

commonMistakes: Do not interpret this object as an owner.
Do not apply -n to every affirmative object.
The context specifies one whole item and a completed purchase.
